purpose: Provide a machine-facing, evaluable ontology of reference & discovery work units for finding, retrieving, evaluating, and synthesizing authoritative knowledge: from reference interview and need typing through search strategy, source selection, query construction, discovery surfaces, citation chaining and grey literature, recall/precision tuning, relevance and bias screening, source appraisal, answer synthesis, reproducible documentation, and alerting.
assumptions: No observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors.
Subdomain of library, archival science & data curation, scoped to reference services and information discovery.
Each node is a session-bounded, evaluable work unit handed off via an artifact.
Patron-facing and systematic/review searching contexts are both in scope.
exclusions: Internal ranking-algorithm engineering and IR system implementation.
Full systematic-review methodology and statistical meta-analysis.
Cataloging, classification, and metadata creation as standalone subdomains.
Detailed information-literacy instruction design beyond search framing.

competency_questions.question: How is a patron's presenting query converted into a fully specified, true information need?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: trace REF_INTERVIEW and INFO_LITERACY nodes plus interview acceptance tests

competency_questions.question: How is the need classified into a search mode (known-item, exploratory, comprehensive, verification)?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NEED_TYPING node label set with rationale

competency_questions.question: How are need boundaries, target, sources, and stopping rule agreed before searching?
How is the search decomposed into concept blocks and an executable plan?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SEARCH_STRATEGY block table and plan present

competency_questions.question: How are databases, repositories, and discovery surfaces chosen to match coverage and currency?
When should controlled vocabulary be used versus free-text keyword searching?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONTROLLED_VOCAB vs KEYWORD_SEARCH conflict axis resolution

competency_questions.question: How is valid Boolean and fielded query logic constructed and translated across databases?
How is the recall/precision tradeoff tuned to the need type with a stopping target?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RECALL_PRECISION tuning record and stopping criterion

competency_questions.question: When are discovery layers versus federated search appropriate, and what are their coverage limits?
How is recall expanded beyond keyword retrieval via citation chaining and grey literature?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CITATION_CHAIN and GREY_LITERATURE outputs and bounds

competency_questions.question: How is a search made reproducible, bounded, and auditable?
How are retrieved results screened for relevance and bias?
How is source authority, accuracy, currency, and bias appraised before use?
How are evaluated sources synthesized into an attributable answer and kept current via alerts?

glossary.definition: Structured dialogue that negotiates a patron's real information need from the presenting query.
Search for a specific, already-identified document or fact.
Open-ended search to learn about or survey a topic space.
Standardized thesaurus/subject-heading terms assigned to documents for consistent retrieval.
Free-text natural-language searching on author wording.
Query using AND/OR/NOT logic, nesting, and field tags.
Proportion of all relevant items that the search retrieves.
Proportion of retrieved items that are relevant.
Web-scale unified search over a pre-harvested central index of catalog and licensed content.
Real-time broadcast querying of multiple native targets with merged results.
Following references backward and citing works forward from seeds (snowballing).
Material not formally published through commercial channels: reports, theses, preprints, datasets.
Frameworks (e.g., ACRL) framing information seeking as iterative, contextual, authority-aware inquiry.
Persisted strategy that re-runs or pushes new matching results for current awareness.
Verbatim record of databases, queries, dates, limits, and counts for reproducibility.

source_registry.description: Heuristic prior estimates for reference & discovery work units, edges, risks, and scores grounded in LIS reference-services and search-methodology practice.
source_registry.citation_or_locator: Rubin & Rubin, Foundations of Library and Information Science (2020); Johnston, Curating Research Data (2017)
grounding_limits: scores are relative heuristic priors not measurements

nodes.definition: Structured negotiation dialogue that converts a patron's initial query into the true, fully-specified information need.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: repeated misnegotiated needs surface in unmet-need audits

pros.claim: Prevents wrong-question search by surfacing the real need before effort is spent
pros.example: Patron asks for 'climate data' but needs local 10-year precipitation series; interview catches it

pros.claim: Improves downstream precision by capturing constraints, format, and currency requirements early
pros.example: Eliciting that only peer-reviewed post-2015 sources count narrows strategy

cons.claim: Over-questioning can frustrate patrons and bias the need toward librarian assumptions
cons.example: Leading questions push patron toward a database the librarian prefers

cons.claim: Asynchronous/chat channels degrade negotiation fidelity
cons.example: Email reference loses turn-taking and nonverbal cues

failure_modes: premature search before need is scoped
acceptance_tests: negotiated need statement restates need in patron-verifiable terms
at least one disambiguating question logged when query is ambiguous
need statement names format, scope, and currency constraints

nodes.definition: Classification of the negotiated need as known-item, exploratory, comprehensive/recall, or verification to select the matching search mode.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: mode/result-type mismatches recur in search post-mortems

pros.claim: Routing to the correct mode prevents recall/precision strategy mismatch
pros.example: Known-item lookup uses fielded search, not broad keyword exploration

pros.claim: Sets the recall/precision target up front for later tuning
pros.example: Comprehensive review need flags recall-maximizing strategy

cons.claim: Hybrid needs resist single labels and can be mis-routed
cons.example: A 'find this paper and everything like it' need is both known-item and exploratory

cons.claim: Mislabeling propagates into strategy and tool choice
cons.example: Tagging an exploratory need as known-item under-searches the space

failure_modes: forces hybrid need into one label
acceptance_tests: need-type label is one of the closed set with a one-line rationale
label is consistent with stated recall/precision target

nodes.definition: Decomposition of the need into concept blocks, synonyms, and a logical plan specifying order, sources, and stopping rules before any query is run.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: strategy revisions cluster when initial yield is poor

pros.claim: A documented plan makes searches reproducible and auditable
pros.example: A logged block strategy lets a colleague rerun and extend the search

pros.claim: Concept decomposition exposes missing synonyms before query failure
pros.example: Breaking 'youth unemployment' into age + employment blocks reveals variant terms

cons.claim: Over-planned strategies ossify and resist iterative discovery
cons.example: Rigid plan ignores promising terms surfaced mid-search

cons.claim: Cost of full strategy is wasteful for trivial known-item needs
cons.example: Documenting a 5-block plan to find one known citation is overhead

failure_modes: no stopping rule causing endless search
plan not revised after poor yield
acceptance_tests: every need concept maps to at least one search block
strategy plan states an explicit stopping rule
plan names target sources and order

nodes.definition: Selection of the databases, indexes, repositories, and discovery surfaces whose coverage, currency, and indexing best match the need.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: missed-database findings appear in coverage audits

pros.claim: Matching source coverage to need prevents systematic miss of key literature
pros.example: Choosing a discipline index over a generic engine surfaces specialist work

pros.claim: Documenting source rationale supports reproducibility and gap analysis
pros.example: Recorded database list shows why a source was excluded

cons.claim: Familiarity bias favors known databases over the best-fit one
cons.example: Defaulting to one vendor platform misses unique-coverage indexes

cons.claim: Coverage claims from vendors can be inflated or stale
cons.example: Advertised date range does not match actual indexed content

acceptance_tests: source list justified against need coverage and currency
at least one alternative source considered and recorded

nodes.definition: Use of thesauri, subject headings, and descriptors to retrieve on assigned concepts independent of author wording.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: precision shifts when descriptor coverage is incomplete

pros.claim: Boosts precision and consistency by retrieving on assigned concepts
pros.example: CV search for 'myocardial infarction' collects all 'heart attack' wordings

pros.claim: Enables explode for hierarchical recall of narrower terms
pros.example: Exploding a broad descriptor pulls all narrower subject terms

cons.claim: Indexing lag and missing descriptors miss recent or emerging topics
cons.example: A new concept has no descriptor yet and is invisible to CV search

cons.claim: Cross-database vocabulary differences break portability
cons.example: One thesaurus's heading has no equivalent in another database

failure_modes: ignores indexing lag for new topics
acceptance_tests: descriptors verified against the live thesaurus
at least one keyword fallback retained for un-indexed concepts

nodes.definition: Free-text natural-language searching across titles, abstracts, and full text, including phrase, proximity, and variant handling.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: recall gaps appear when synonym coverage is thin

pros.claim: Catches new, interdisciplinary, and un-indexed concepts CV misses
pros.example: Free-text finds an emerging term before any descriptor exists

pros.claim: Full-text and proximity reach content not in subject metadata
pros.example: Proximity query finds a concept discussed only in body text

cons.claim: Synonym and spelling variation cause silent recall loss
cons.example: Missing a British spelling drops a whole set of relevant records

cons.claim: Homographs and ambiguity inflate false hits
cons.example: 'Mercury' retrieves planet, element, and mythology records

acceptance_tests: synonym set covers major term variants
phrase/proximity used where word order matters

nodes.definition: Construction of valid Boolean and field-restricted query logic (AND/OR/NOT, nesting, field tags, truncation) that executes the strategy.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: logic errors recur in query-translation reviews

pros.claim: Explicit logic gives precise, reproducible control over set size
pros.example: Nested OR-of-synonyms AND-ed across blocks yields a clean result set

pros.claim: Field restriction sharpens precision by scoping where terms match
pros.example: Restricting a name to author field removes subject false hits

cons.claim: Mis-nested logic or wrong precedence silently corrupts results
cons.example: Missing parentheses make AND bind before OR and drop relevant records

cons.claim: Syntax is non-portable across database platforms
cons.example: Truncation symbol differs by vendor and breaks on copy-paste

failure_modes: operator precedence error from missing nesting
acceptance_tests: query parses and runs without syntax error on target database
operator nesting reviewed for precedence correctness
each platform variant validated before execution
revisit_triggers: result count implausibly high or low

nodes.definition: Deliberate tuning of the strategy toward recall or precision against the need type and an explicit stopping/sufficiency target.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: tuning is revisited when sufficiency target is not met

pros.claim: Aligning the tradeoff to need type avoids wasted effort or missed evidence
pros.example: Exhaustive review tunes for recall; quick fact lookup tunes for precision

pros.claim: Explicit stopping target prevents over- or under-searching
pros.example: A documented saturation rule justifies ending the search

cons.claim: Recall and precision trade off; pushing one degrades the other
cons.example: Broadening synonyms raises recall but floods results with noise

cons.claim: True recall is unknowable without a gold set
cons.example: Without a reference set, recall is only estimated

acceptance_tests: tradeoff direction matches need-type recall/precision target
an explicit stopping or saturation criterion is recorded
revisit_triggers: result set unmanageably large or empty

nodes.definition: Use of unified discovery interfaces and central indexes that search across catalog and licensed content through a single relevance-ranked entry point.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: coverage opacity surfaces when discovery misses known items

pros.claim: One entry point lowers barrier and surfaces cross-collection results
pros.example: A single search returns books and articles for a novice patron

pros.claim: Facets enable fast post-search refinement without re-querying
pros.example: Limiting to peer-reviewed and last 5 years via facets

cons.claim: Opaque central-index coverage and ranking hide what is missed
cons.example: A key database is not in the central index and is silently absent

cons.claim: Relevance ranking can bury precise results under popular ones
cons.example: Highly relevant niche article ranked far below popular reviews

failure_modes: assumes full coverage of all licensed content
acceptance_tests: central-index coverage of needed sources verified
critical needs cross-checked against a native database

nodes.definition: Broadcast querying of multiple native targets in real time with merged results, used when no shared central index covers the needed sources.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: latency/dedup failures recur in federated logs

pros.claim: Reaches live targets not covered by any shared central index
pros.example: Broadcasts to a niche provider absent from the discovery index

pros.claim: Returns current native results without harvest lag
pros.example: Real-time hit on a just-added record before any index update

cons.claim: Slow, lowest-common-denominator queries and weak ranking
cons.example: Broadcast collapses advanced syntax to a basic AND across targets

cons.claim: Duplicate and inconsistent merging degrades the result set
cons.example: Same article appears thrice from three overlapping targets

acceptance_tests: dropped/timed-out targets reported to the user
merge dedup verified on a sample

nodes.definition: Backward and forward citation following (snowballing) from seed documents to expand recall beyond keyword retrieval.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: snowball stopping is revisited when new seeds keep appearing

pros.claim: Finds relevant work that keyword and CV searches miss
pros.example: Forward chaining surfaces recent papers citing a seminal seed

pros.claim: Complements database search to raise recall for reviews
pros.example: Backward+forward snowballing recovers off-vocabulary studies

cons.claim: Citation bias and incomplete indexes skew the expanded set
cons.example: An influential paper's critics outside the index are never reached

cons.claim: Unbounded snowballing explodes the candidate set
cons.example: Each iteration multiplies candidates without a stopping rule

acceptance_tests: seed set justified against the need
snowball iterations bounded by an explicit stopping rule

nodes.definition: Targeted retrieval of non-commercially-published and database-invisible material: reports, theses, preprints, datasets, and deep-web sources.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: reporting bias is reassessed when only published sources are found

pros.claim: Reduces publication and reporting bias by reaching unpublished evidence
pros.example: A null-result report excluded from journals is recovered for a review

pros.claim: Surfaces current and practitioner knowledge ahead of formal publication
pros.example: A preprint provides results months before the journal version

cons.claim: Hard to find, unstable URLs, and uneven quality complicate use
cons.example: A cited report's hosting site disappears and the source is lost

cons.claim: No standard indexing makes systematic coverage difficult
cons.example: Grey sources are scattered across registries with no shared index

acceptance_tests: grey sources captured with provenance and access date
search of at least one grey-literature registry documented
revisit_triggers: only published sources found for a bias-prone topic

nodes.definition: Systematic screening of retrieved results against need criteria to judge topical and need-relevance and triage the keep/discard decision.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: screening criteria drift is caught in consistency audits

pros.claim: Consistent criteria make screening reproducible and reduce bias
pros.example: A documented relevance rubric lets two screeners agree

pros.claim: Early triage controls downstream workload and noise
pros.example: Discarding off-topic hits at title stage saves full-text review

cons.claim: Premature discard loses recall; lenient keep inflates noise
cons.example: Strict abstract screening drops a relevant study with a vague abstract

cons.claim: Single-screener judgment carries reviewer bias
cons.example: One screener's topic interpretation skews inclusion

acceptance_tests: relevance criteria documented and applied uniformly
ambiguous items flagged rather than silently discarded
revisit_triggers: recall check finds wrongly discarded items

nodes.definition: Appraisal of authority, accuracy, currency, and bias of retrieved sources before they are accepted as answer evidence.

excluded: full systematic critical appraisal of methods

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: credibility errors surface when cited sources are later retracted

pros.claim: Filtering on authority prevents propagating misinformation as answers
pros.example: Catching a predatory-journal article keeps it out of the answer set

pros.claim: Provenance checks support defensible, citable conclusions
pros.example: Verified author affiliation and source date strengthen the answer

cons.claim: Authority heuristics can entrench bias against valid outsider work
cons.example: Dismissing a preprint solely for lacking journal status

cons.claim: Appraisal is effort-heavy and can stall fast reference needs
cons.example: Full authority workup is disproportionate for a quick fact

acceptance_tests: authority, currency, and bias assessed for accepted sources
predatory or low-quality sources flagged with rationale
provenance recorded for each cited source

nodes.definition: Integration of evaluated sources into a coherent, attributable answer or curated result set that addresses the negotiated need.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: answer-need mismatches recur in satisfaction follow-ups

pros.claim: Delivers an attributable answer rather than an unstructured result dump
pros.example: Synthesized summary with citations directly answers the patron's need

pros.claim: Explicit gap statement sets honest expectations
pros.example: Noting what could not be found prevents false confidence

cons.claim: Synthesis can over-claim certainty beyond source support
cons.example: Stating a firm conclusion from conflicting weak sources

cons.claim: Curation choices can drop minority but valid evidence
cons.example: Summarizing away a dissenting source for a cleaner answer

failure_modes: answer does not map to negotiated need
acceptance_tests: answer maps explicitly to the negotiated need statement
every claim is attributed to an evaluated source
residual gaps stated explicitly
revisit_triggers: patron indicates answer misses the need

nodes.definition: Capture of databases, query strings, dates, limits, and result counts so the search can be reproduced, audited, and updated.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: irreproducible searches are exposed in update or audit attempts

pros.claim: Makes searches reproducible, auditable, and updatable
pros.example: A logged strategy lets a review be rerun a year later for an update

pros.claim: Supports transparent reporting and peer scrutiny
pros.example: PRISMA search report lets reviewers verify the search

cons.claim: Documentation overhead is heavy for simple ready-reference
cons.example: Full search log is disproportionate for a one-line factual lookup

cons.claim: Logs drift from reality if not captured at run time
cons.example: Reconstructed-after-the-fact log misstates the actual query

acceptance_tests: each database query, date, and limit recorded verbatim
result counts and dedup logged
revisit_triggers: search must be updated or rerun

nodes.definition: Persisting search strategies as saved searches and alerts/feeds for ongoing current-awareness and reproducible re-runs.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: alert drift surfaces when results stop matching the need

pros.claim: Automates current-awareness so new results arrive without re-searching
pros.example: An alert delivers each new paper on a tracked topic

pros.claim: Saved strategies make periodic re-runs reproducible
pros.example: A saved search reruns identically each quarter

cons.claim: Stale alerts drift from evolving needs and miss new terms
cons.example: An alert built on old synonyms misses newly coined terms

cons.claim: Alert fatigue causes users to ignore feeds
cons.example: Too-broad alert floods inbox and is muted

acceptance_tests: saved search reproduces the validated query
alert cadence and scope matched to need
revisit_triggers: alert volume too high or zero

nodes.definition: Application of information-literacy frameworks (e.g., ACRL) to frame searching as iterative, contextual, and authority-aware inquiry.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: framing gaps surface when patrons cannot transfer skills

pros.claim: Frames searching as iterative inquiry, improving transfer and judgment
pros.example: Treating authority as constructed helps a patron weigh a blog vs a study

pros.claim: Aligns reference work with teaching and lifelong-learning goals
pros.example: ACRL framing turns a search into a transferable skill lesson

cons.claim: Frameworks are abstract and hard to operationalize per query
cons.example: 'Authority is constructed' gives no concrete query-level action

cons.claim: Over-theorizing can slow concrete reference delivery
cons.example: Lengthy framing delays a simple factual answer

acceptance_tests: framing translated into at least one concrete search action
authority lens applied to source evaluation

nodes.definition: Faithful adaptation of one validated strategy across databases with differing syntax, fields, and vocabularies while preserving semantics.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: translation errors recur when result counts diverge implausibly

pros.claim: Preserves search semantics so multi-database coverage stays comparable
pros.example: Re-mapping descriptors keeps a strategy equivalent across two indexes

pros.claim: Validation catches silent semantic drift across platforms
pros.example: A test query confirms the translated logic returns expected anchors

cons.claim: Naive copy-paste corrupts logic, fields, and vocabulary silently
cons.example: Pasting one database's truncation symbol breaks it in another

cons.claim: Some constructs have no equivalent target and must be approximated
cons.example: A proximity operator absent in a target weakens the translation

acceptance_tests: each translated query validated against expected anchor records
field and vocabulary mappings documented per platform
untranslatable constructs flagged with an approximation note
revisit_triggers: result counts diverge implausibly across platforms

nodes.definition: Detection and mitigation of bias introduced by source choice, language, vocabulary, ranking, and screening across the discovery process.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: bias is reassessed when results skew to one language/region/source

pros.claim: Surfaces and mitigates systematic blind spots in the search
pros.example: Adding non-English sources corrects a language-skewed result set

pros.claim: Improves equity and completeness of the evidence base
pros.example: Balancing databases avoids over-representing one vendor's coverage

cons.claim: Full bias control is costly and never fully achievable
cons.example: Translating queries into many languages is resource-prohibitive

cons.claim: Mitigation can introduce noise that lowers precision
cons.example: Broadening for equity floods the set with marginal records

acceptance_tests: major bias sources (language, source, ranking) explicitly assessed
at least one mitigation action recorded or justified as N/A
coverage balance across sources documented

nodes.definition: An explicit shared agreement on need boundaries, recall/precision target, sources, and stopping rule that governs and bounds the whole search.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: scope creep is caught when effort exceeds the agreed boundary

pros.claim: Bounds the search and prevents scope creep and endless effort
pros.example: A signed scope with a stopping rule ends a search defensibly

pros.claim: Aligns patron and searcher expectations before effort is spent
pros.example: Agreeing 'last 10 years, English, 3 databases' avoids later disputes

cons.claim: Rigid scope can exclude legitimately emergent needs
cons.example: A fixed scope blocks a relevant adjacent topic found mid-search

cons.claim: Formal contracting is overhead for trivial requests
cons.example: A scope agreement is disproportionate for a one-fact lookup

failure_modes: scope drifts without a logged change
acceptance_tests: scope contract names boundaries, target, sources, and stopping rule
any scope change recorded with rationale

edges.why_related: need type can be classified only after the need is negotiated
edges.example: cannot label known-item vs exploratory before the real need is known
edges.resolution_rule: source dominates: do not type before interview output is confirmed

edges.why_related: scope boundaries derive from the negotiated need
edges.risk_of_conflict: unbounded search if scope precedes need
edges.example: scope contract restates negotiated need boundaries
edges.resolution_rule: finalize scope only after interview need statement

edges.why_related: need type sets the recall/precision target inside scope
edges.example: exploratory type drives a recall-leaning scope target
edges.resolution_rule: type label must precede scope target setting

edges.why_related: strategy mode is chosen from the need type
edges.example: known-item type triggers fielded strategy
edges.resolution_rule: do not formulate strategy before type is set

edges.why_related: scope bounds which concepts, sources, and stopping rules the strategy may use
edges.example: scope of '3 databases, 10 years' caps the strategy plan
edges.resolution_rule: scope dominates; strategy revisions require a logged scope change

edges.why_related: source set depends on the need type and recall target
edges.example: comprehensive need selects multiple subject indexes
edges.resolution_rule: select sources after type is known

edges.why_related: strategy plan informs which sources are searched first and why
edges.example: plan orders subject index before generic discovery
edges.resolution_rule: sequence: draft strategy then finalize source order

edges.why_related: descriptor selection operationalizes the strategy's concept blocks
edges.example: each strategy block maps to thesaurus descriptors
edges.resolution_rule: build CV terms from strategy blocks

edges.why_related: free-text terms operationalize the strategy's synonym lists
edges.example: strategy synonyms become free-text query terms
edges.resolution_rule: derive keywords from strategy synonym lists

edges.why_related: Boolean query combines descriptors into executable logic
edges.example: descriptors OR-ed within block, AND-ed across blocks
edges.resolution_rule: CV terms feed into Boolean construction

edges.why_related: Boolean query combines free-text terms with operators
edges.example: keywords with proximity inside Boolean blocks
edges.resolution_rule: keywords feed into Boolean construction

edges.why_related: controlled-vocabulary and free-text retrieval pull precision vs recall in opposite directions
edges.risk_of_conflict: over-reliance on one mode skews results
edges.example: CV-only misses new terms; keyword-only floods noise
edges.resolution_rule: combine both; weight toward need-type target (recall->keyword-heavy, precision->CV-heavy)

edges.why_related: Boolean structure changes the size and precision of the result set
edges.example: loosening operators raises recall and lowers precision
edges.resolution_rule: tune logic to meet the recall/precision target

edges.why_related: need type sets the recall vs precision target
edges.example: comprehensive type demands recall-leaning tuning
edges.resolution_rule: set target from need type before tuning

edges.why_related: the precision/recall balance changes the screening load and false-hit rate
edges.example: recall-leaning search raises screening volume
edges.resolution_rule: accept the screening cost implied by the chosen target

edges.why_related: results must be retrieved before they can be relevance-judged
edges.example: judge only after the query set is complete
edges.resolution_rule: run query before screening

edges.why_related: discovery-layer use depends on which sources its central index covers
edges.example: discovery index must include the chosen databases
edges.resolution_rule: verify discovery coverage of selected sources

edges.why_related: central-index discovery and broadcast federated search are competing access strategies
edges.example: use discovery for indexed content, federation for uncovered live targets
edges.resolution_rule: prefer central-index discovery; use federation only for targets absent from the index

edges.why_related: federated targets are chosen from the selected sources not in any central index
edges.example: federate only the niche provider missing from discovery
edges.resolution_rule: select federation targets from coverage gaps

edges.why_related: seed-based chaining follows after an initial strategy yields seeds
edges.example: forward-chain from the best seeds the strategy found
edges.resolution_rule: chain after initial retrieval; bound iterations

edges.why_related: chaining raises recall and changes the precision balance
edges.example: each snowball round adds candidates
edges.resolution_rule: bound chaining by the recall/precision stopping target

edges.why_related: grey-literature search complements the database strategy for bias reduction
edges.example: add registry and report searches to the plan
edges.resolution_rule: include grey search when reporting bias is a risk

edges.why_related: grey-literature coverage changes the publication/reporting bias of the set
edges.example: including unpublished reports reduces a positive-result skew
edges.resolution_rule: require grey search where bias risk is high

edges.why_related: translation adapts the validated Boolean query to each database
edges.example: re-map field tags and truncation per platform
edges.resolution_rule: translate only a validated source query

edges.why_related: target databases for translation come from the selected source set
edges.example: translate for each selected database's syntax
edges.resolution_rule: translate per selected platform

edges.why_related: differing controlled vocabularies constrain faithful translation
edges.example: one index's descriptor has no equivalent in another
edges.resolution_rule: re-map vocabulary; flag untranslatable descriptors

edges.why_related: topical relevance is judged before authority appraisal of kept items
edges.example: screen for topic first, then appraise authority
edges.resolution_rule: relevance-judge then credibility-appraise

edges.why_related: synthesis uses only credibility-appraised sources
edges.example: exclude predatory sources before synthesizing
edges.resolution_rule: synthesize only from appraised sources

edges.why_related: synthesis integrates the relevance-judged result set
edges.example: include only relevance-kept items in the answer
edges.resolution_rule: synthesize from screened set

edges.why_related: the negotiated need bounds what the synthesized answer must address
edges.example: answer must map back to the original negotiated need
edges.resolution_rule: need statement dominates answer scope

edges.why_related: executed queries must be captured for reproducibility
edges.example: log each query string, date, and count at run time
edges.resolution_rule: document at execution time

edges.why_related: documentation records which databases were searched
edges.example: log every database with run dates
edges.resolution_rule: record all searched sources

edges.why_related: alerts persist a validated executable query for ongoing awareness
edges.example: save the validated query as a recurring alert
edges.resolution_rule: build alerts only from validated queries

edges.why_related: information-literacy framing shapes how the interview elicits authority-aware needs
edges.example: authority-as-constructed lens prompts source-quality questions
edges.resolution_rule: translate framing into concrete interview questions

edges.why_related: the authority-as-constructed frame guides credibility appraisal criteria
edges.example: frame informs what counts as authority for this need
edges.resolution_rule: apply the authority lens to appraisal criteria

edges.why_related: the agreed scope and stopping rule bound how far tuning may go
edges.example: scope's stopping rule caps recall expansion
edges.resolution_rule: scope stopping rule dominates tuning extent

edges.why_related: the scope contract is part of the reproducible search record
edges.example: log the scope and any scope change with the search
edges.resolution_rule: record scope alongside the search log

edges.why_related: detected bias triggers revisiting and rebalancing the source set
edges.example: language skew prompts adding non-English sources
edges.resolution_rule: loop back to source selection; stop when coverage is balanced or budget is reached

edges.why_related: poor relevance yield triggers strategy revision
edges.example: high false-hit rate prompts tighter blocks
edges.resolution_rule: loop to strategy; stop when precision target met or max 3 revisions

edges.why_related: an answer that misses the need triggers re-negotiation
edges.example: patron says the answer misses the point
edges.resolution_rule: loop to interview; stop after one clarification round or escalate

conflict_axes.trigger: need requires both comprehensive coverage and a manageable, precise result set
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: need type sets the target: comprehensive/review needs favor recall, ready-reference favors precision; tune to the agreed stopping target
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: unknown true recall on a high-stakes review need
conflict_axes.example: a systematic review tunes for recall while accepting heavy screening

conflict_axes.trigger: a concept is both indexed and emerging/interdisciplinary
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: combine both; lead with CV for precision-stable concepts and keyword for new/un-indexed concepts, weighted to the need-type target
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: emerging topic with no descriptor on a high-recall need
conflict_axes.example: new technology term has no descriptor, so keyword carries recall while CV anchors precision

conflict_axes.trigger: a one-stop discovery search is convenient but its coverage and ranking are opaque
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: use discovery for breadth and novices; require native advanced search for high-recall or high-stakes needs where coverage must be verified
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: high-stakes comprehensive need relying solely on opaque discovery
conflict_axes.example: a review searcher confirms results in native databases rather than trusting the discovery index

conflict_axes.trigger: a fast answer is wanted but rigorous documentation, appraisal, and bias control take time
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: match rigor to stakes per the scope contract; never skip credibility or bias control for high-stakes needs even under time pressure
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: high-stakes need forced into a ready-reference timeframe
conflict_axes.example: a clinical question is not answered from the top web hit despite urgency

conflict_axes.trigger: a relevant adjacent topic or new concept emerges after scope is fixed
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: scope governs effort; expand only via a logged scope change agreed with the requester, not silently mid-search
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: emergent concept materially changes the need
conflict_axes.example: snowballing surfaces a new subtopic that requires a documented scope amendment

conflict_axes.trigger: strict authority filters risk excluding valid unpublished or outsider evidence
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: appraise authority as constructed and contextual; do not exclude grey/preprint sources solely for publication status without an accuracy/bias check
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a key result exists only in grey literature
conflict_axes.example: a relevant null-result report is appraised on merit rather than dismissed for being unpublished

conflict_axes.trigger: relevance ranking is trusted in place of human relevance and authority judgment
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: treat ranking as a triage aid, not a verdict; human relevance and authority judgment dominate for accepted evidence
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: high-stakes answer drawn only from top-ranked results
conflict_axes.example: a searcher inspects lower-ranked but precisely relevant items rather than only the top 10

conflict_axes.trigger: full documentation and per-database translation cost effort disproportionate to simple needs
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: scale documentation to need type: full logging and translation for reviews, lightweight capture for ready-reference
conflict_axes.example: a systematic search is fully logged while a quick fact lookup records only the source

conflict_axes.trigger: teaching iterative-inquiry framing slows immediate answer delivery
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: deliver the needed answer first; apply framing as transferable instruction when context and patron readiness allow
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: patron explicitly needs only a fast answer
conflict_axes.example: a librarian answers the question, then briefly models the authority lens for next time

edge_cases.trigger: a translated query references a field or operator not supported by the target database
edge_cases.failure_mode: query silently runs with dropped logic and wrong results
edge_cases.example: a proximity operator absent in a platform is dropped, broadening the set
edge_cases.detection_method: validate translated query against expected anchor records per platform

edge_cases.trigger: presenting query accepted verbatim without negotiation
edge_cases.failure_mode: entire search answers the wrong question
edge_cases.example: patron asks for 'statistics' but needs a specific local dataset
edge_cases.detection_method: check that need statement restates need in patron-verifiable terms

edge_cases.trigger: missing nesting makes AND bind before OR
edge_cases.failure_mode: result set silently loses relevant records
edge_cases.example: a OR b AND c retrieves far fewer records than (a OR b) AND c
edge_cases.detection_method: review operator nesting and compare set sizes against expectation

edge_cases.trigger: a needed database is not in the discovery central index
edge_cases.failure_mode: relevant content is silently absent from results
edge_cases.example: a niche subject index is excluded from the central index and never appears
edge_cases.detection_method: cross-check known items against native databases

edge_cases.trigger: snowballing runs without a stopping rule
edge_cases.failure_mode: candidate set explodes and screening becomes infeasible
edge_cases.example: each iteration triples candidates with no convergence
edge_cases.detection_method: track new-relevant yield per iteration against a stopping threshold
resolution: stop when new-relevant yield falls below threshold

edge_cases.trigger: a high-risk node lacks acceptance tests or human-review flag
edge_cases.failure_mode: unappraised or biased sources enter the answer unchecked
edge_cases.example: credibility node ships without an authority-check acceptance test
edge_cases.detection_method: validator checks high-risk nodes have acceptance_tests and human_review_required

edge_cases.trigger: the search is finalized before bias and credibility gates pass
edge_cases.failure_mode: an irreproducible or biased search is locked as complete
edge_cases.example: answer delivered before credibility appraisal is done
edge_cases.detection_method: check that synthesis lock follows credibility and bias gate passage

edge_cases.trigger: strategy-relevance feedback loop revises without convergence
edge_cases.failure_mode: endless re-search with no stopping point
edge_cases.example: each revision marginally changes precision and loops again
edge_cases.detection_method: count revision iterations against the max-iteration cap

edge_cases.trigger: the CV-vs-keyword tradeoff is modeled as a dependency rather than a conflict
edge_cases.failure_mode: the planner enforces a false prerequisite and skips the needed balance
edge_cases.example: a graph forces CV before keyword as a dependency, dropping the tradeoff
edge_cases.detection_method: check that CV/keyword relation is a conflict edge with negative tension

edge_cases.trigger: strategy is prioritized before the interview that scopes it
edge_cases.failure_mode: effort is spent on a strategy for an unscoped need
edge_cases.example: priority_order places strategy before its interview prerequisite

edge_cases.trigger: a saved alert keeps running on outdated vocabulary
edge_cases.failure_mode: new relevant results are silently missed by the alert
edge_cases.example: an alert built on old synonyms misses a newly coined term
edge_cases.detection_method: periodically compare alert yield and vocabulary against current terms

edge_cases.trigger: results skew to one language, region, or single vendor source
edge_cases.failure_mode: a systematically biased evidence base is treated as complete
edge_cases.example: an English-only search misses key non-English studies
edge_cases.detection_method: assess coverage balance across language, region, and source

workflow.objective: negotiate and fully specify the true information need
acceptance_tests: need statement names format, scope, and currency
at least one disambiguating question logged when ambiguous
workflow.do_first_because: all downstream effort depends on having the correct need; wrong need is the highest-rework failure

workflow.objective: classify need type and agree scope, target, sources, and stopping rule
gates: scope contract names boundaries, target, sources, and stopping rule
acceptance_tests: need-type label from closed set with rationale
explicit stopping rule recorded
workflow.do_first_because: a bounded, typed scope prevents scope creep and routes the correct search mode before strategy work

workflow.objective: decompose into concept blocks and select fit-for-need sources
gates: every concept maps to a block
source list justified against coverage and currency
acceptance_tests: strategy plan states an explicit stopping rule
at least one alternative source considered
workflow.do_first_because: a documented strategy and source set make later querying reproducible and reduce rework

workflow.objective: build and validate executable Boolean/fielded queries combining CV and keyword terms
entry_criteria: strategy plan and source list available
gates: query parses and runs without syntax error
acceptance_tests: synonym set covers major variants
descriptors verified against the live thesaurus
exit_criteria: query validated on the primary database
workflow.do_first_because: a validated base query is the prerequisite for translation, alerts, and tuning

workflow.objective: faithfully translate the validated query across selected databases
gates: each translation validated against expected anchor records
acceptance_tests: field and vocabulary mappings documented per platform
untranslatable constructs flagged
workflow.do_first_because: comparable multi-database coverage requires validated translations before execution

workflow.objective: execute searches and expand recall via discovery surfaces, chaining, and grey literature
gates: discovery coverage of needed sources verified
snowball iterations bounded by a stopping rule
acceptance_tests: dropped/timed-out federated targets reported
grey sources captured with provenance
exit_criteria: expansion reaches the recall stopping target
workflow.do_first_because: recall expansion must finish before tuning and screening so the candidate pool is complete

workflow.objective: tune the recall/precision balance to the need type and stopping target
acceptance_tests: explicit stopping/saturation criterion recorded
set size is manageable for screening
exit_criteria: tuning meets the agreed target or triggers a scope change
workflow.do_first_because: tuning the set before screening avoids re-screening an oversized or undersized pool

workflow.objective: screen results for relevance and assess and mitigate bias
gates: relevance criteria documented and applied uniformly
acceptance_tests: ambiguous items flagged not silently dropped
at least one bias mitigation recorded or justified N/A
workflow.do_first_because: relevance and bias must be controlled before authority appraisal and synthesis

workflow.objective: appraise authority and synthesize an attributable answer to the negotiated need
gates: authority, currency, and bias assessed for accepted sources
answer maps explicitly to the negotiated need
acceptance_tests: predatory/low-quality sources flagged
every claim attributed to an evaluated source
residual gaps stated
exit_criteria: human review passed for high-stakes synthesis
workflow.do_first_because: answer quality depends on appraised sources and must pass review before being locked and delivered

workflow.objective: finalize the reproducible search record and set up current-awareness alerts
gates: each query, date, and limit recorded verbatim
saved search reproduces the validated query
acceptance_tests: result counts and dedup logged
alert cadence and scope matched to need
exit_criteria: search log complete and alerts active
workflow.do_first_because: the reproducible record and alerts are finalized last, after the search is stable, to capture the actual executed strategy

priority_rationale.notes: all search work depends on the correct need
framing shapes elicitation and appraisal across the workflow
routes the search mode and recall/precision target
bounds the whole search and prevents scope creep
central plan that most downstream nodes consume
executable query whose errors corrupt all results
faithful multi-database coverage depends on it
reaches sources outside the central index
ongoing awareness after the search is stable

dominance_rules.rule: rigor dominates speed for high-stakes needs
dominance_rules.required_action: appraise authority and bias before answering even when fast delivery is requested
dominance_rules.example: a clinical question is not answered from the top web hit
interview must precede strategy even if strategy seems higher value

dominance_rules.trigger: a non-heuristic evidence label is asserted without an eligible source
dominance_rules.rule: correct evidence labeling dominates numeric precision
dominance_rules.example: an 'observed' precision claim with no dataset is relabeled heuristic

dominance_rules.trigger: search is about to be locked before gates pass
dominance_rules.rule: QA gates dominate locking and delivery
dominance_rules.required_action: keep lock at draft until screening, credibility, and bias gates pass
dominance_rules.example: answer is not finalized until credibility appraisal completes

dominance_rules.trigger: automation/ranking would replace human judgment on accepted evidence
dominance_rules.rule: human relevance and authority judgment dominate ranking automation
dominance_rules.required_action: treat ranking as triage; human-judge accepted items
dominance_rules.example: a searcher inspects beyond the top-ranked results

dominance_rules.trigger: a relevant source exists only in grey literature
dominance_rules.rule: inclusiveness with appraisal dominates publication-status filtering
dominance_rules.required_action: appraise grey sources on accuracy/bias instead of excluding for status
dominance_rules.example: a null-result report is appraised on merit, not dismissed

dominance_rules.trigger: strategy/source set must change after detected bias
dominance_rules.rule: bias correction dominates convenience of a fixed source set within budget
dominance_rules.required_action: rebalance sources via a logged scope change
dominance_rules.example: language skew triggers adding non-English sources

dominance_rules.trigger: CV-vs-keyword tradeoff is modeled as a dependency
dominance_rules.rule: correct conflict modeling dominates convenient dependency encoding
dominance_rules.required_action: encode the tradeoff as a conflict edge with a resolution rule
dominance_rules.example: CV/keyword relation is a signed conflict, not a prerequisite

dominance_rules.trigger: JSON validity conflicts with denser prose
dominance_rules.rule: strict JSON validity dominates prose richness and density
dominance_rules.required_action: reduce density before sacrificing valid JSON
dominance_rules.example: trim examples rather than emit invalid JSON

dominance_rules.trigger: documentation overhead pressures a high-stakes search
dominance_rules.rule: reproducibility dominates effort-saving for mandated searches
dominance_rules.required_action: fully log queries, dates, and counts for review/legal/clinical needs
dominance_rules.example: a systematic search is fully logged despite the overhead

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-risk decision would be made without review
dominance_rules.rule: human review dominates automation for high-risk or irreversible steps
dominance_rules.required_action: require human sign-off for high-risk nodes before lock
dominance_rules.example: bias-blindspot and wrong-question cases require human review

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not formulate strategy before the need is negotiated and confirmed
anti_rework_rules.rationale: wrong-need searches are the most expensive rework
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: strategy work begins with an unconfirmed need statement
anti_rework_rules.example: planning blocks before patron confirms the need

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not search before scope, target, and stopping rule are agreed
anti_rework_rules.rationale: unbounded searches overrun effort and resist defensible stopping
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: queries run with no recorded stopping rule
anti_rework_rules.example: searcher cannot say when the search is done

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not build Boolean logic before term sets (CV and keyword) are prepared
anti_rework_rules.rationale: logic built on incomplete terms must be rebuilt
anti_rework_rules.example: missing-variant recall gaps appear after execution

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not translate across databases before the base query is validated
anti_rework_rules.rationale: translating an unvalidated query propagates errors to every platform
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: translations derive from an unvalidated query
anti_rework_rules.example: the same logic error appears in all database variants

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not screen results before tuning the recall/precision balance
anti_rework_rules.rationale: screening an untuned set wastes effort on an oversized or undersized pool
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: screening starts on an unmanaged set size

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not synthesize an answer before sources are credibility-appraised
anti_rework_rules.rationale: answers from unappraised sources must be redone or retracted
anti_rework_rules.example: a cited source is later found predatory or retracted

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not finalize the search before bias is assessed and mitigated
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a biased evidence base invalidates the whole answer
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: results skew to one language/region/source unexamined
anti_rework_rules.example: reviewers reject the search for coverage bias

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not hard-lock the answer before human review passes for high-stakes needs
anti_rework_rules.rationale: premature locks force costly post-lock change control
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: lock set to hard before review threshold passes

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not expand scope silently; record any scope change before continuing
anti_rework_rules.rationale: silent scope drift corrupts reproducibility and effort tracking
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: new subtopic searched without a logged scope change
anti_rework_rules.example: final search differs from the agreed scope with no record

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not lock priority order before dependencies are verified acyclic
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a priority inversion forces re-execution in the wrong order
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: priority places a dependent before its prerequisite
anti_rework_rules.example: strategy ranked before its interview prerequisite

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not capture documentation after the fact; log at execution time
anti_rework_rules.rationale: reconstructed logs misstate the actual queries and counts
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: search log written from memory after the session
anti_rework_rules.example: logged query does not match what was actually run

action: prioritize high-risk and reference-integrity defects first
acceptance_tests: queue ordered by risk

action: apply formula recompute and reference fixes

action: accept residual low-risk defects within tolerance
